title: Resin code 1: PET
identification: Clear or lightly tinted, thin and crinkly; the base often has a small dot where it was moulded.
cleaning_prep: Empty and rinse, squash flat, put the cap back on unless told otherwise.

not_accepted: bottles that held oil-based chemicals or motor oil

notes: PET is the most widely recycled plastic; it becomes new bottles, polyester fibre and strapping.
Designed for single use: do not reuse drink bottles for hot drinks or leave them in hot cars.

title: Resin code 2: HDPE
title_ar: رمز الراتنج 2: البولي إيثيلين عالي الكثافة
identification: Opaque, slightly waxy and stiff; often white or coloured.
cleaning_prep: Rinse out product, leave to drain and replace the cap.

not_accepted: containers that held motor oil, pesticides or solvents

notes: HDPE is tough and widely recycled into pipes, crates and outdoor furniture.
Bottles that held detergent or bleach must never be reused for food, drink or pets.

title: Resin code 3: PVC
identification: Rigid pipes or soft, rubbery films; blister packs are often PVC bonded to foil.
cleaning_prep: Separate from other plastics; clean offcuts of pipe can go to builders' recycling.

recycling.stream: General waste or specialist construction recycling
accepted: large clean pipe offcuts at specialist recyclers
not_accepted: household recycling bins in most places

notes: PVC releases hydrogen chloride and dioxins when burned: never burn it.
Reuse rigid PVC (pipe sections) for garden and storage projects instead.

title: Resin code 4: LDPE
title_ar: رمز الراتنج 4: البولي إيثيلين منخفض الكثافة
identification: Soft and stretchy; bags stretch before they tear.
cleaning_prep: Shake out crumbs, keep dry, bundle bags inside one bag.

recycling.stream: Plastic bag collection point (often at supermarkets)
not_accepted: kerbside bins in most areas (films jam sorting machines)

notes: Bags are best reused: as bin liners, for plarn crafts or returned to supermarket collection.

title: Resin code 5: PP
identification: Stiff but flexible, often semi-opaque; lids flex without cracking.
cleaning_prep: Scrape and rinse out food; greasy takeaway boxes need a hot soapy wash.

not_accepted: containers with food left in them

notes: PP is increasingly recycled into crates, bins and car parts.
Sturdy PP tubs are among the best plastics to reuse for storage.

title: Resin code 6: PS (polystyrene)
identification: Foam that breaks into beads, or brittle clear plastic that snaps with a crack.
cleaning_prep: Keep packaging foam clean and dry; some electronics shops take it back.

recycling.stream: General waste unless a specialist foam collection exists
accepted: clean packaging foam at specialist collection points

notes: Never heat or burn polystyrene: it releases styrene fumes.
Clean packaging foam can be reused for posting parcels.

title: Resin code 7: other plastics
identification: Anything that does not fit codes 1-6, including mixtures and bioplastics.
cleaning_prep: Rinse and check whether the supplier runs a return scheme (common for large water bottles).

recycling.stream: Supplier return scheme or general waste
accepted: returnable water cooler bottles through the supplier

notes: Water cooler bottles are designed to be returned and refilled: give them back to the supplier.
